Ayodhyā-kāṇḍa
------------------------------------------
This is the second book of the famous epic Rāmāyaṇa of वाल्मीकि.
See RĀMĀYAṆA for details.

Ayodhyā
(‘invincible’)
------------------------------------------
Ayodhyā is the first of the seven holy cities of ancient India considered to be capable of giving मुक्ति or लिबेरतिओन्. It is also famous because of its association with राम, the son of दशरथ, considered to be an इन्चर्नतिओन् of God.
Manu, the first traditional king of India, is said to have founded the city of अयोध्या as his capital. It was 12 yojanās long and 3 yojanās broad. (1 yojanā = 15 kilometres.) The galaxy of great rulers who ruled from here includes इक्ष्वाकु, Māndhātā, हरिश्चन्द्र, भगीरथ, दिलीप and रघु. The great ṛṣi वसिष्ठ and his family were the hereditary priests of the royal families of अयोध्या.
King विक्रमादित्य of Vikram Śaka fame is said to have raised a temple at the birth-place of राम and also rebuilt the city.
The city of Sāketas, well-known during the time of बुद्ध, has been identified with अयोध्या.
Both Fa-Hien (A.
